newsitem.title: UK: WORLD BONDS - SHORT END PERIPHERAL EUROPE BECKONS.
newsitem.headline: WORLD BONDS - SHORT END PERIPHERAL EUROPE BECKONS.

text.p: Investors searching for a bright spot in the gloom of German interest rate uncertainty should seek out the short end of peripheral Europe, economists said on Tuesday.
With short end EMU convergence trades in vogue, any dips at that end of Spanish and Portuguese bond markets in particular are an ideal buying opportunity for the brave investor, they added.
"This uncertainty (in German interest rates) is probably going to cause a bit of a problem for peripherals," said Phyllis Reed, European bond strategist at BZW in London.
"They will tend to suffer, but we would look at that as a big buying opportunity for the front end of those markets.
"In the end we're going to have to see a closing up of the interest rate gap if European Monetary Union (EMU) is really going to happen," she said.

The one problem is predicting when the gap at the short end will close, with the guessing game on German interest rates making it even harder for peripherals such as Italy and Spain to bring their interest rates down further, analysts said.

"Will the Bank of Italy turn around and cut rates when Buba is on a tightening cycle -- I find it very hard to believe that they can cut in those circumstances," said Huw Roberts, European bond strategist at NatWest Markets.

European bond markets rebounded on Tuesday after the Bundesbank set its repo at an unchanged fixed rate of 3.0 percent. There had been some speculation the German central bank might move to a variable repo to support the mark against the dollar and other European currencies.
That speculation shows no sign of abating, despite Tuesday's move, leaving markets to grapple with considerable uncertainty in the meantime.
With that background, Roberts said he was still bearish on the short end of the German curve. "Euromarks still look a bit vulnerable so curve flattening trades make sense," he said.
David Brickman, European bond strategist at Yamaichi International Europe in London, also said the short end of Bunds many come under pressure.

"Certainly over the next few months there will be uncertainty every week, with Bunds trading very closely against the currency -- as it weakens, the short end in particular will come under pressure," he said.

He said in a weak mark environment, peripheral bond markets may be able to outperform Bunds. This, plus the short end convergence plays, means Spain and Portugal offer some of the best opportunities in Europe, he said.

"Spain and Portugal offer the best, safest returns -- those are where there is still value in Europe, they are two of the higher yielders that are most likely to be part of EMU on time...and you can have Spain and Portugal in without Italy," said Brickman.
He said with a lot of convergence already having taken place at the long end, many investors were looking at the two, three and four year sectors of the higher yielding curves.
"The place where we're going to see convergence now is at the front end -- particularly given we've only got eight months left for a decision on EMU," he said.
